newsitem.title: KENYA: Export inflows boost Kenya shilling vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Export inflows boost Kenya shilling vs dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling rose marginally against the dollar on exporter inflows but was weaker versus all other major currencies, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.135 against the dollar from 56.16 on Tuesday, and of 87.81 to the pound from 87.41.

"The third day of the week saw a very active interbank trading session with rates temporarily breaking through the 56 level, though the shilling drive soon lost steam and could not sustain its power," a dealer said.

"The market initially opened at 56.10/20, then moved up to 56.15/25 in the face of importer demand," a commercial banker said. "Midday saw a large inflow of dollars to the market, which coupled with sentiment, drove rates down to as low as 55.80/05."

Another dealer added "The dollar seems more vulnerable to shilling consolidation as the week goes by. Dollar buying interest from oil corporations at the 56 level seems to help support the greenback at the moment."
Dealers said overnight money market rates remained above 20 percent as money was taken out of the market for tax payments.
